hints: For each row, count consecutive empty cells ending at that row in every column.
Use a monotonic stack to find the largest rectangle in each histogram.
analogy: Every empty rectangle has a bottom edge; at that edge its columns form bars at least as tall as the rectangle.
example: In a 2 by 3 empty grid, the largest building covers all 6 cells.
algorithm: Scan rows, updating each column height to zero at a tree or increasing it at an empty cell. For each histogram, use an increasing stack of bar indices; when a shorter bar arrives, pop taller bars and compute their maximal width. Flush the stack at the end of the row and retain the largest area.
correctness: The height array records exactly the available empty cells above each position. The stack computes the widest interval for which each popped height is a valid minimum, so it considers an optimal rectangle at every possible bottom row.
complexity: For n rows and m columns, O(nm) time and O(m) space.
